grandparents_cupboard.reason: Butter, golden syrup, brown sugar, oats, seeds, egg and pears are all plain cupboard and garden foods.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item in any mainstream supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: Only a saucepan and a 20cm square tin are needed, and the technique is simple melting and pressing.

works.reason: The ratios are standard for a flapjack, the egg helps it hold with the wet pear topping, and 30 minutes at 180°C will set and colour it for 12 bars.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is enough to melt, stir, core and slice two pears and press it all into the tin, and the 30-minute bake matches the step.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, and nothing unlisted appears in the steps.

seasonal_feel.reason: Early September pears laid across the top are the feature of a baked afternoon snack that suits late summer.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oat-heavy bars with seeds, egg and fresh fruit make a reasonable family snack rather than pure sugar.
